chunks: Ḥanān ibn Sadīr narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:

Every sin is expiated by being killed in the way of Allah, except debt; there is no expiation for it except repayment, or that its holder be satisfied, or that the one to whom the right belongs forgive.

key_terms.الْأَدَاءُ: repayment and fulfillment of what is owed
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: the due right owed to someone
key_terms.الْقَتْلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: being killed in the way of Allah; martyrdom in Allah’s cause
key_terms.ذَنْبٍ: a sin or offense requiring expiation
key_terms.صَاحِبُهُ: its owner, meaning the creditor or holder of the right
key_terms.يُكَفِّرُهُ: removes it as expiation and atonement

ai.seo_question: Can martyrdom expiate all sins, including unpaid debt?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that even the immense merit of being killed in the way of Allah does not remove the liability of debt owed to others. Financial rights remain binding until they are repaid, the creditor is satisfied, or the rightful claimant forgives.
